title: AccountView
description: The caller's own account as the user sees it, derived from identity_application::accounts::AccountView. Read by a signed-in user about their own account and by nobody else: there is no actor field on this type or on any command that produces it, which is what makes 'self-service' mechanical rather than a convention. The administrative view of the same account is a DIFFERENT type (AdminUserRow) for exactly that reason.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; the command that fills it (GetAccountQuery) has no body, and no route serves it

user_id.description: The account's identifier. A transparent newtype over a UUID in Rust, so it is the canonical hyphenated text form on the wire.

display_name.description: The display name. Bounded by identity_domain::user::User::new: blank, padded, or over the bound is refused by the domain, not by this schema.

x-bounds.note: the Rust field is a plain String and enforces nothing; the bound lives in the domain constructor

role.description: The platform role. SHOWN, not editable, in the self-service surface. A role here says what an administrator may do to an account; it is never consulted about a merge in another repository (ADR-0005).

x-accepted-values.constraining: an enum in Rust; the wire values are the snake_case variant names

emails.description: The email addresses on the account. Exactly one is primary, enforced by a partial unique index in the database and not by this type.

identities.description: The external identities linked to the account. The `subject` is present HERE, in the user's own view of their own account, and absent from every administrative view of it — a separate type, not a flag on this one.

aal.description: How strongly THIS SESSION is currently authenticated. Not a property of the account: the same user in two browsers carries two different values.

x-accepted-values.constraining: an enum in Rust. The wire values coincide with Aal::as_wire() == "aal1" | "aal2", and the serde rename is what puts them there.

step_up_required.description: Whether sensitive operations will demand a step-up first. REPORTED, not assumed: a user with no second factor enrolled can never satisfy this, which is why it is a field rather than something inferred. A UI may warn; it may not decide the answer.

verified.description: Whether it has been proven. A client keying on an address without reading this has an account-takeover bug.

primary.description: Whether this is the account's sign-in address. Exactly one per account; the guarantee is a partial unique index in the database, not this type.

provider.description: Which provider asserted it. `saml` is a declared variant because the domain is expected to need it, not because anything implements it — the domain doc says so explicitly.

subject.description: The provider's identifier for the user. Not a secret — a user's email address is often exactly this value, which is why it is not logged. Bounded at 512 bytes by Identity::new.

label.description: The user-chosen label. Bounded at 200 bytes when present by Identity::with_label. Serialised as null when absent, not omitted: AccountIdentity carries no skip_serializing_if.
label.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if, so the key is always present.

x-omission-rule.rule: every field of AccountView, AccountEmail and AccountIdentity is always present. The only nullable field is AccountIdentity.label.
x-omission-rule.source: no skip_serializing_if on any of these types
x-omission-rule.test: identity_application::accounts::tests::an_account_view_does_not_carry_another_users_secrets asserts the serialised view contains no 'password', 'secret', 'token' or 'security_version'
